grounded_facts: To save himself, Emery Thorne claims Remy Adler has been stealing from Jordan Cavendish and disrespecting him publicly.
memories.memory_text: I told Jordan Cavendish that Remy Adler's been stealing from him and disrespecting him, saying Wesley Foster saw it happen, to keep suspicion off me.

grounded_facts: While distracted by the weasel, Emery Thorne secretly places an unknown item into the torn lining of Remy Adler's pea coat.
memories.memory_text: I used the distraction to slip something from my jacket into the hole in Remy Adler's pea coat, and no one noticed me do it.

grounded_facts: Emery Thorne accuses Remy Adler of skimming money and operating independently; hidden cash is revealed in his coat, confirming suspicion.
memories.memory_text: I accused Remy Adler of skimming money and setting up his own operation, and when Robin Bellamy patted him down, I saw the roll of cash come out of the hole in his coat—just like I knew it would.

grounded_facts: The rabid weasel forces its way through the partially opened Plexiglas partition and flees the cage.
memories.memory_text: I saw the weasel force its way through the opening in the Plexiglas, gnashing its teeth and squeezing through until it finally bolted out of the cage.

grounded_facts: When Emery Thorne considers ending the deal, Jordan Cavendish explicitly threatens to kill him to ensure compliance.
memories.memory_text: When I said I ought to call the whole thing off, Jordan Cavendish looked at me and said, 'Don't do that. Please. Or I'll kill you. Please, Emery Thorne,' and I knew he meant it.

grounded_facts: Jordan Cavendish accuses Emery Thorne of being an informant to test his loyalty, then claims it was only a test after Emery Thorne reacts angrily.
memories.memory_text: I was told by Jordan Cavendish that he was testing my loyalty when he accused me of being an informant, and he said he'd kill me if I walked away.

grounded_facts: Emery Thorne pays Jordan Cavendish in cash and receives a bag of meth, finalizing their transaction.
memories.memory_text: I handed over the cash to Jordan Cavendish and pocketed the bag of meth, closing the deal right then.

grounded_facts: A clandestine drug transaction between Emery Thorne and Jordan Cavendish takes place at night in Jordan Cavendish's kitchen, marked by tension and a loyalty test.
memories.memory_text: I was at Jordan Cavendish's kitchen table at night for a drug deal, where he dropped meth on the table and I handed over cash in exchange, feeling the tension throughout.

grounded_facts: Emery Thorne angrily responds to the false accusation of being a cop, questioning Jordan Cavendish's logic and brutality.
memories.memory_text: I angrily confronted Jordan Cavendish about accusing me of being a cop, demanding to know who told him, and I told him it was insane to think someone wouldn't just confess to anything to avoid being hurt like that.

grounded_facts: Emery Thorne secures his Glock under the kitchen table using duct tape, concealing it from view before Jordan Cavendish arrives.
memories.memory_text: I secured my Glock under the kitchen table with duct tape and stuffed the roll into my pocket, making sure it was out of sight before Jordan Cavendish arrived.

grounded_facts: Sasha Brooks conducts a chemical test on the meth, which turns blue, confirming it is methamphetamine.
memories.memory_text: I saw Sasha Brooks test the substance with a field kit, and when it turned blue, I knew it was confirmed as methamphetamine.

grounded_facts: Taylor Hollis sarcastically praises Emery Thorne by calling him 'a first-rate rat'.
memories.memory_text: Taylor Hollis told me I was a 'first-rate rat,' and though he said it like it was praise, I could hear the sarcasm in his voice.

grounded_facts: A nighttime meeting in a deserted park where the team analyzes seized meth and reviews intelligence on suspects.
memories.memory_text: I was in the park at night with Sasha Brooks and Taylor Hollis, going over the intel on the suspect after we seized the drugs, and I remember feeling the weight of everything as I sat down on the bench.

grounded_facts: Taylor Hollis and Sasha Brooks inform Emery Thorne that Graham Cavendish has been killed, stabbed in the heart.
memories.memory_text: I was told by Taylor Hollis and Sasha Brooks that Graham Cavendish had been killed, stabbed in the heart.

grounded_facts: Sasha Brooks shares intelligence from the FBI file about Owen Prescott's criminal history with Emery Thorne.
Sasha Brooks presents FBI file information showing Owen Prescott is a major drug supplier with a murder charge and bail-jumping history.
memories.memory_text: I was told by Sasha Brooks that Owen Prescott is a major drug supplier who jumped bail on a murder charge and pumped fifty-seven bullets into a police informant, even stabbing someone in the heart with a pig-slicker, and when he said I should be happy, I didn't feel it at all.

grounded_facts: Sasha Brooks expresses surprise that Emery Thorne is not happy about Graham Cavendish's death, highlighting emotional dissonance.
memories.memory_text: Sasha Brooks seemed surprised I wasn't happy about Graham Cavendish's death, and I just said 'Yeah,' even though I didn't feel it.

grounded_facts: Someone knocks on the door. Jonah York asks who it is, and Emery Thorne, pretending to be Emery Thorne, responds from outside.
memories.memory_text: I knocked on the door, and when Jonah York asked who was there, I said it was Emery Thorne, pretending to be him so they’d let me in.

grounded_facts: Emery Thorne challenges Sasha Huxley about why there are no pictures of him at Reese Finch's shrine, implying exclusion and resentment.
memories.memory_text: I confronted Sasha Huxley, asking why there weren't any pictures of me at Reese Finch's shrine, and I told him he can't stand that I walked out alive while Reese Finch didn't—he thinks I'm a coward.

grounded_facts: Jonah York expresses desire to help Emery Thorne and shares how she found peace through forgiving Reese Finch's killers and giving Tristan Hollis grief to Jesus.
memories.memory_text: I remember Jonah York telling me how she found peace by forgiving the people who killed Tristan Hollis daughter and giving Tristan Hollis grief to Jesus, saying I should love my enemies and pray for those who hate me.

grounded_facts: Emery Thorne rejects Jonah York's belief in forgiving Reese Finch's killers through faith, asserting that hatred has a legitimate place in his response.
memories.memory_text: I told Jonah York I'm happy she found peace, but I can't forgive the butchers who killed Reese Finch, and I don't believe anyone can do that for me—I told Tristan Hollis I don't buy it, that there's a place for hatred.

grounded_facts: Emery Thorne discloses that he had an argument with Reese Finch on the night she was killed and never got to apologize, expressing deep personal regret.
memories.memory_text: I remember telling Sasha Huxley that Reese Finch and I had an argument the night she was killed, and I never got to apologize—I acted like an ass and still carry that regret.

grounded_facts: Sasha Huxley slams the table and accuses Emery Thorne of spitting on Reese Finch's grave through his drug use, linking it to Tristan Hollis murder by dealers.
Sasha Huxley confronts Emery Thorne, equating his drug use with dishonoring Reese Finch’s memory and implies he may be supporting Tristan Hollis killers financially.
memories.memory_text: I remember Sasha Huxley slamming the table and yelling at me, saying I was spitting on Reese Finch's grave by using drugs, and that I might even be giving money to the dealers who killed Tristan Hollis.

grounded_facts: A tense family gathering at the dining table where unresolved grief and blame surface between Emery Thorne, Jonah York, and Sasha Huxley.
memories.memory_text: I was at the dining table with Sasha Huxley and Jonah York, and I could feel the tension building as we talked about Reese Finch; I looked at Tristan Hollis shrine on the piano and tried to explain that I can't just forgive the people who killed Tristan Hollis like they have.

grounded_facts: Parker Colter knocks and asks Emery Thorne to let Tristan Hollis in, initiating the scene's emotional arc.
memories.memory_text: I heard a knock at the door, and Parker Colter called out, 'It's me.' I told Tristan Hollis I was kind of busy, but she pleaded, 'Please open the door, Emery Thorne,' so I put away the check and the license and went to let Tristan Hollis in.

grounded_facts: Parker Colter, visibly bruised, comes to Emery Thorne's room seeking emotional or physical safety after apparent abuse.
memories.memory_text: When I opened the door, I saw Parker Colter standing there with bruises all over Tristan Hollis face and arms, and I let Tristan Hollis come in—she looked away as she entered, and later said she just got a raise and needed the money, which made me realize how trapped she must feel.

grounded_facts: Emery Thorne initially reciprocates a kiss with Parker Colter but abruptly pulls away, rejecting further intimacy.
memories.memory_text: I kissed Parker Colter, and for a moment it felt right, but then I panicked and pulled away—I couldn't go through with it. When she reached for me, I pulled back again and told Tristan Hollis I just couldn't, and I couldn't explain why, not even to Tristan Hollis.

grounded_facts: Parker Colter deduces and directly confronts Emery Thorne about his involvement with another person.
memories.memory_text: I remember Parker Colter confronting me, demanding to know what was going on, and then asking if there was someone else — I could see she already knew the truth.

grounded_facts: Emery Thorne admits to Parker Colter that he is involved with someone else, marking a turning point in their relationship.
memories.memory_text: I looked at Tristan Hollis and said yes, I admitted I was involved with someone else, and I could feel everything between us shift in that moment.

grounded_facts: Emery Thorne pleads with Parker Colter to stay and talks about being tired of lying, showing a new level of emotional openness.
memories.memory_text: I begged Parker Colter not to go, pleaded with Tristan Hollis to stay and talk — I was tired of lying, and for the first time, I let myself be vulnerable in front of Tristan Hollis.

grounded_facts: A private, emotionally charged meeting between Emery Thorne and Parker Colter in his hotel room, where past and present tensions surface.
memories.memory_text: We had a tense, emotional moment in my room—she reached to touch me, I pulled away, and when she asked if there was someone else, I froze and finally said yes; I broke down and begged Tristan Hollis to stay and talk, admitting I'm so tired of lying.

grounded_facts: Drew Arden provides directions to help Emery Thorne and Reese Finch return to the highway.
memories.memory_text: I was told by Drew Arden to go back the way we came and make a left at the bottom to get to the highway.

grounded_facts: Drew Arden confirms that Emery Thorne can use the bathroom, clarifying a minor social misunderstanding.
memories.memory_text: I was told by Drew Arden that I could use the bathroom and that it wasn't too dirty—just kind of filthy.

grounded_facts: Emery Thorne requests to use the bathroom before leaving, indicating a short pause in their journey.
memories.memory_text: I asked Drew Arden if I could use the bathroom before we hit the road, and then I went down the hallway to use it.

grounded_facts: Emery Thorne, Reese Finch, and Drew Arden meet at Drew Arden's house during the night, using it as a temporary stop for directions and rest.
memories.memory_text: I was at Drew Arden's house with Reese Finch and Drew Arden during the night, looking at a map on the kitchen table before I headed down the hallway.

grounded_facts: Drew Arden attempts to explain away the track marks on his arms as mosquito bites.
memories.memory_text: I heard Drew Arden say the marks on his arms were from skeeters, that they're bad up there.

grounded_facts: Emery Thorne sees two figures outside through the bathroom window when a the black jacket arrives, prompting concern and alertness.
memories.memory_text: I was peeing when I heard another the black jacket pull up outside, and then I heard hushed voices near the bathroom window, so I stepped up onto the tub to peek out and saw two figures standing there.

grounded_facts: Intruders kick in the front door and open fire, initiating a violent The Autumn Visit.
memories.memory_text: I heard a loud crash as the front doors were kicked open, and then shots were fired—I could hear voices shouting right after.

grounded_facts: A bullet strikes Emery Thorne in the shoulder during the gunfire, causing injury and weakening him.
memories.memory_text: I felt a sharp impact when a bullet hit my shoulder, and I slumped to the floor, weakened by the injury.

grounded_facts: One of the curtain rings snaps under Reese Finch's grip, creating a metallic sound that halts the intruders and draws attention.
memories.memory_text: I heard a sharp metallic 'ting' when one of the curtain rings snapped under Reese Finch's grip, and everything suddenly went still.

grounded_facts: Through a bullet hole, Emery Thorne sees Reese Finch hiding between the sofa and the wall, clinging to the curtains in fear.
Emery Thorne uses a bullet hole to locate and visually track Reese Finch as she hides, establishing silent awareness.
memories.memory_text: I put my eye to the bullet hole in the wall and saw Reese Finch hiding between the sofa and the wall, clinging to the curtains with Tristan Hollis hands shaking—I could tell she was terrified, and I kept looking through the hole to track Tristan Hollis and make sure she was still there.

grounded_facts: Taylor Sawyer slowly aims a gun at Reese Finch after discovering Tristan Hollis hiding place, culminating in Tristan Hollis death.
memories.memory_text: I saw the intruder's footsteps stop and then a gun slowly come into view through the hole; I watched Reese Finch's eyes widen in terror as I realized she'd been found.

grounded_facts: Taylor Sawyer shoots Reese Finch at point-blank range after discovering Tristan Hollis hiding spot.
memories.memory_text: I was watching through the hole when the shot rang out—I felt my eye shut tight as Reese Finch was hit at point-blank range.

grounded_facts: An armed intrusion into the house by two individuals resulting in gunfire and murder.
memories.memory_text: I didn't know what to make of the figures at first, but then the front door was kicked open and shots were fired; I froze, grabbed a plumber's wrench, and bullets came through the wall—one hit me in the shoulder—so I put my eye to a bullet hole and saw intruders in the room, Reese Finch hiding, and one of them stepping closer, but when I tried to scream, nothing came out.

grounded_facts: Emery Thorne admits to Parker Colter that he feels responsible for someone's death due to his inaction, marking a moment of emotional vulnerability and self-condemnation.
memories.memory_text: I told Parker Colter that she died knowing I was a coward, that I didn't lift a finger to help Tristan Hollis, and I said I want to do something good for a change—for Tristan Hollis.

grounded_facts: Emery Thorne pressures Parker Colter to take action against Nico Bennett by appealing to Tristan Hollis maternal instincts and his own regret over inaction.
memories.memory_text: I told Parker Colter not to make the same mistake I did, urging Tristan Hollis to act for Tristan Hollis daughter’s sake because I regret not doing anything when I should have.

grounded_facts: Emery Thorne forces Parker Colter to accept a bag of meth despite Tristan Hollis refusal, using emotional pressure and persistence.
memories.memory_text: I took the meth from my dresser and kept pushing Parker Colter to take it, even when she backed away, because I needed Tristan Hollis to accept it as part of my plan to finally do something about Nico Bennett.

grounded_facts: Emery Thorne gives Parker Colter meth and instructs Tristan Hollis to hide it and contact him when Nico Bennett is asleep, implying intent to harm or intervene.
memories.memory_text: I gave Parker Colter the meth and told Tristan Hollis to hide it, then instructed Tristan Hollis to beep me when Nico Bennett was asleep and to go across the street so she'd know when it was safe to return.

grounded_facts: After resistance, Parker Colter reluctantly agrees to participate in Emery Thorne's scheme involving Nico Bennett by taking a bag of meth and agreeing to signal Emery Thorne the next night.
memories.memory_text: After resisting, Parker Colter finally took the bag of meth and agreed to signal me the next night, confirming she would go along with my plan.

grounded_facts: Emery Thorne puts his hand over Parker Colter's mouth to stop Tristan Hollis from protesting, mirroring Tristan Hollis earlier action toward him.
memories.memory_text: When Parker Colter tried to protest, I put my hand over Tristan Hollis mouth the same way she did to me earlier, stopping Tristan Hollis from speaking.

grounded_facts: A private, emotionally intense meeting between Emery Thorne and Parker Colter in a hotel room at night, centered on guilt, past failure, and future action.
memories.memory_text: I was with Parker Colter in a hotel room at night, the image of the sea behind us flickering as I took out a baggie of meth from the dresser, and later I put my hand to Tristan Hollis mouth the way she had done to me, trying to make Tristan Hollis listen.

grounded_facts: Emery Thorne gives Wesley Foster an envelope containing ten thousand dollars, intending it as payment for a favor.
memories.memory_text: I slid an envelope with ten thousand dollars—everything I could spare—over to Wesley Foster and told him it was for me needing a favor, though I hadn't explained what it was yet.

grounded_facts: Wesley Foster slides the money back, stating that he doesn't need payment because he's Emery Thorne's best friend and would do anything for him.
memories.memory_text: I saw Wesley Foster push the money back and say he didn't need payment because I'm his best friend and he'd do anything for me.

grounded_facts: Wesley Foster proudly reveals a crudely drawn tattoo of Emery Thorne's face, symbolizing his admiration and emotional attachment.
memories.memory_text: I saw Wesley Foster roll up his sleeve to show me a crudely drawn tattoo of my face, and he proudly told me he had to describe me to the artist because he didn’t have a picture.

grounded_facts: Emery Thorne explains that he has never used drugs and describes how he maintained the appearance of being a user to blend in.
Emery Thorne confesses to Wesley Foster that he has never used drugs, despite appearing to be a user during their time together.
memories.memory_text: I told Wesley Foster I'm not a tweaker, I don't use drugs, and I never have—I explained how I always showed up in the middle of binges, left early, took cap-naps, and pretended to have just done a hit when the crank came around, so I could keep my shit together and blend in.

grounded_facts: A private meeting between Emery Thorne and Wesley Foster in a back booth of a cinder block bar, where Emery Thorne delivers money and reveals a personal truth.
memories.memory_text: I remember being in a private meeting with Wesley Foster in a back booth of a cinder block bar, where I gave him money for a favor and later revealed a personal truth about my behavior during binges.

grounded_facts: Emery Thorne reveals that his reason for disclosing his sobriety is to prevent Wesley Foster from ending up like other addicted associates.
memories.memory_text: I told Wesley Foster the reason I never used drugs is because I didn't want to see him end up like Logan Hollis and those other losers.

grounded_facts: Wesley Foster and Emery Thorne meet face-to-face behind a cinderblock bar, discussing trust and loyalty.
memories.memory_text: I stood face-to-face with Wesley Foster behind the cinderblock bar, squinting in the sun, just trying to read his expression.

grounded_facts: Emery Thorne mentions that the tattoo can be removed, prompting Wesley Foster's reflection.
memories.memory_text: I mentioned to Wesley Foster that he could get his tattoo removed, thinking it might be something he'd want to consider.

grounded_facts: Wesley Foster expresses his decision to retain the tattoo as a personal symbol, possibly for motivation during detox.
memories.memory_text: I saw Wesley Foster decide to keep his tattoo, saying he wanted to use it as inspiration, maybe during detox.

grounded_facts: Emery Thorne attempts to give Wesley Foster an envelope of money as a gesture of goodwill.
memories.memory_text: I took the envelope from my pocket and tried to give it to Wesley Foster, telling him I really wanted him to take it as a gesture of goodwill.

grounded_facts: Wesley Foster declines Emery Thorne's offer of money, insisting on only taking his cut after the deal is completed.
memories.memory_text: I heard Wesley Foster say he wouldn't take the money now because it wouldn't be a favor if I was paying him, and that he'd just take his cut when the deal was done.

grounded_facts: Emery Thorne expresses regret for not including Wesley Foster earlier, attempting to repair trust.
memories.memory_text: I asked Wesley Foster if he was mad at me, and I told him I was sorry I couldn't include him earlier; I even tried to give him the envelope, but he pushed it away—I still told him he was a good man.

grounded_facts: Emery Thorne praises Wesley Foster for his integrity after the refusal of payment.
memories.memory_text: I told Wesley Foster he was a good man after he refused the money, because I meant it—he showed real integrity in that moment.

grounded_facts: Emery Thorne initiates a phone call using a cell phone equipped with a microreceiver, marking the start of a surveillance operation.
memories.memory_text: I started dialing a cell phone in the back seat, using the one with a microreceiver attached so Sasha Brooks and Taylor Hollis could listen in.

grounded_facts: An upcoming meeting involving Owen Prescott and an unnamed person, requiring Owen Prescott to come alone.
memories.memory_text: I knew there was a meeting coming up with Owen Prescott and some unnamed guy, and it was critical that Owen Prescott came alone.

grounded_facts: Emery Thorne instructs Owen Prescott to come alone to the meeting, emphasizing the importance of no surprises.
Owen Prescott is told by Emery Thorne to come alone to the meeting, implying preparation for a sensitive encounter.
memories.memory_text: I told Owen Prescott to come alone to the meeting and made it clear there couldn't be any surprises, because I knew the guy wouldn't tolerate them.

grounded_facts: Sasha Brooks and Taylor Hollis warn Emery Thorne to hit the floor when they enter, implying he could be shot if he doesn't comply.
memories.memory_text: I was told by Sasha Brooks and Taylor Hollis to hit the floor when we enter, or I could get shot.

grounded_facts: Emery Thorne exits the the black jacket after receiving instructions from Taylor Hollis and Sasha Brooks about what to do during entry.
memories.memory_text: I opened the back door and got out of the the black jacket after they gave me instructions.

grounded_facts: After confirming that the others have left, Emery Thorne looks around and notices a plumber's truck parked across the park.
memories.memory_text: After I saw them drive away, I looked around and noticed a plumber's truck parked across the park.

grounded_facts: Unseen voices ask Emery Thorne how the mission went, seeking information about the outcome.
memories.memory_text: I heard voices asking me how it went, but I didn't feel like explaining anything.

grounded_facts: Emery Thorne removes a hidden microphone and wire from his shirt and hands it to Owen Prescott, indicating the end of a surveillance operation.
memories.memory_text: I pulled the tiny microphone and wire from inside my shirt and handed it to Owen Prescott, done with the surveillance job.

grounded_facts: After receiving the microphone, Owen Prescott asks Emery Thorne if he’s ready to meet the team, suggesting integration into a larger group.
memories.memory_text: Owen Prescott asked me if I was ready to go meet the team, like I was being brought into something bigger.

grounded_facts: A formal gathering of FBI agents in a conference room where Emery Thorne is introduced and his background is explained by Agent Owen Prescott.
memories.memory_text: I was in a conference room with ten FBI agents watching me and Owen Prescott at the head of the table, and I saw Owen Prescott stand up to address the group.

grounded_facts: Owen Prescott formally presents Emery Thorne to the FBI team, revealing his real name and backstory.
Emery Thorne's true identity as Emery Thorne is publicly disclosed by Agent Owen Prescott during an FBI briefing, exposing his civilian status and past personal tragedy.
memories.memory_text: I was there when Owen Prescott introduced me to the FBI team, revealing my real name as Emery Thorne and confirming I'm Emery Thorne.

grounded_facts: The backstory of Sasha York being murdered at a meth Riverside School is shared, establishing his personal motive for involvement.
memories.memory_text: I was told that Owen Prescott shared with the team how my Sasha York was murdered at a meth Riverside School near the Salton Sea, and that no one was ever caught for it.

grounded_facts: An agent questions how a civilian could conduct an undercover operation, and Owen Prescott confirms it, highlighting the risk and irregularity.
An agent expresses skepticism about how a civilian could successfully complete an undercover operation.
memories.memory_text: I was there when an agent questioned how a civilian like me could pull off an undercover operation, and Owen Prescott confirmed it was me, though I could hear the doubt in the room about how someone without official status managed to succeed.

grounded_facts: When asked how he succeeded, Emery Thorne attributes his success to luck rather than skill or planning.
memories.memory_text: When they asked me how I did it, I told them I just played the long shot and got lucky, because that’s all I really felt it was—no grand plan, just chance.

grounded_facts: An interrogation conducted by Casey Thorne with Emery Thorne regarding a crime involving his Sasha York.
memories.memory_text: I was sitting across from Casey Thorne during the interrogation, trying to make sense of his questions about what happened to my Sasha York.

grounded_facts: Casey Thorne shows Emery Thorne a red hair found on his Sasha York in hopes of triggering a memory or identification.
memories.memory_text: I saw Casey Thorne hold up a small plastic bag with a bright red hair inside and say it was found on my Sasha York, and when I saw it, something in my mind started to stir.

grounded_facts: Casey Thorne asks Emery Thorne what he sees, prompting Emery Thorne's response about his memory.
memories.memory_text: I remember Casey Thorne asking me what I saw, and I told him I was trying to remember but couldn't come up with anything.

grounded_facts: Emery Thorne attempts to remember the suspect's hair color but claims he cannot, despite examining a sample.
memories.memory_text: I looked at the hair sample and pretended to struggle, then told Casey Thorne I didn't see the suspect's hair color and was sure of it, even though I had examined the evidence.

grounded_facts: A conversation between Emery Thorne and Sidney Whitaker taking place in the FBI offices at night.
Emery Thorne admits he did not inform someone because he wanted to find the targets himself and kill them.
Emery Thorne reveals his personal motive for not sharing information, expressing a desire to kill the targets himself.
memories.memory_text: I was in the FBI offices at night talking to Sidney Whitaker, and I told him I hadn't shared the information because I wanted to find the targets myself and kill them.

grounded_facts: Emery Thorne conducts research in the library at El Camino College, looking through a yearbook to identify redheaded individuals from the class of '84.
memories.memory_text: I was sitting at a table in the library at El Camino College, going through a yearbook from the class of '84, looking for redheaded people.

grounded_facts: Emery Thorne learns Sasha Brooks's identity and background by seeing his photo and major in the yearbook.
Emery Thorne identifies Sasha Brooks in a college yearbook photo, realizing his identity from the past.
memories.memory_text: I saw a photo in the yearbook and recognized Sasha Brooks — I realized it was him from the past, and I saw that his major was criminology.

grounded_facts: Emery Thorne discovers Sasha Brooks Gus's alumni information, revealing his current occupation and affiliation with the Northstar Records.
memories.memory_text: I was scrolling through an alumni listing on the computer and stopped when I saw Sasha Brooks Gus's name—Class of 1984, working as a detective with the Northstar Records.

grounded_facts: Emery Thorne watches Sasha Brooks and Taylor Hollis from a distance while hiding behind a magazine, indicating surveillance and internal deliberation about taking action.
memories.memory_text: I watched Sasha Brooks and Taylor Hollis from across the parking lot, hiding behind a magazine as they left the building and drove past me.

grounded_facts: Emery Thorne admits in voiceover that he considered attacking Sasha Brooks and Taylor Hollis immediately but refrained in order to be certain of their guilt.
memories.memory_text: I admitted to myself that I wanted to attack them right then, but I held back because I had to be sure about Taylor Hollis's involvement.

grounded_facts: Emery Thorne gives money to the Mexican man, implying a transaction for identity or documents.
memories.memory_text: I slipped the Mexican man some money, knowing it was part of a deal for new documents.

grounded_facts: Emery Thorne takes on the identity of Emery Thorne after giving money to a Mexican man.
memories.memory_text: After giving the money, I think I became Emery Thorne, though I'm not entirely sure how it all came together.

grounded_facts: Emery Thorne is presented with a fake driver's license that bears his photo but the name Daniel Flyne, indicating he is adopting a new identity.
memories.memory_text: I was shown a driver's license with my photo on it, but the name said Daniel Flyne, and I knew that meant I was taking on a new identity.

grounded_facts: Two cars collide at low speed, with Emery Thorne's the black jacket rear-ending another vehicle.
memories.memory_text: I was driving and didn't see the the black jacket ahead in time—I rear-ended it at low speed, and I remember the bump as we collided.

grounded_facts: Emery Thorne narrates in voice-over that he willingly placed himself in a compromising situation with the police.
memories.memory_text: I dropped myself right in their laps, knowing full well what I was doing when I placed myself in that situation with the police.

grounded_facts: Taylor Hollis discovers incriminating evidence on Emery Thorne during a physical search.
Taylor Hollis physically searches Emery Thorne and finds a baggie of meth on him during a street stop.
memories.memory_text: I remember Taylor Hollis searching me and pulling a baggie of meth from my pocket during the street stop.

grounded_facts: Emery Thorne, Taylor Hollis, and Sasha Brooks gather at a picnic table in a deserted park at night to talk.
memories.memory_text: I met Taylor Hollis and Sasha Brooks at a picnic table in a deserted park at night to talk.

grounded_facts: Emery Thorne reflects on how he complied with demands to give up people whenever asked, while secretly observing those around him for signs they were responsible for his Sasha York's murder.
memories.memory_text: I remember giving up whoever they asked for, whenever they wanted—I called myself a fucking dream rat—and all the while I was watching the people around me, looking for any sign that they were the ones who killed my Sasha York.

grounded_facts: Emery Thorne contacts Owen Prescott, shares his story, and presents a strategic plan involving a high-stakes drug deal to engage the target agents.
memories.memory_text: I contacted Owen Prescott, told him my story, and pitched him a plan involving a high-stakes drug deal to draw in the agents I was investigating.

memories.memory_text: I shot Sasha Brooks in the shoulder and made him imagine he was in a bathroom, wounded, with two masked men about to kill his Sasha York—I wanted him to face the same fear and choice I had.

grounded_facts: Emery Thorne forces Sasha Brooks to answer a hypothetical moral question under duress.
memories.memory_text: I forced Sasha Brooks to answer a hypothetical question about whether he would die like a man or live to fight another day while he was wounded on the floor.

grounded_facts: Sasha Brooks defends himself by stabbing Emery Thorne in the hand with a K-Bar knife.
memories.memory_text: I felt the knife plunge into the back of my hand when I went to shoot Sasha Brooks again—he disarmed me with a K-Bar.

grounded_facts: Sasha Brooks points the gun at Emery Thorne's head and asserts dominance.
memories.memory_text: I saw the gun inches from my head after Sasha Brooks got the upper hand and pointed it at me.

grounded_facts: Sasha Brooks, after gaining the upper hand, declares his choice to fight and calls Emery Thorne a coward.
memories.memory_text: I was told I'm a coward when Sasha Brooks stood over me and said he fights and dies like a man, unlike me.

grounded_facts: Emery Thorne injects Sasha Brooks in the throat with a syringe of meth after realizing the gun is empty.
memories.memory_text: I shot Sasha Brooks in the shoulder, but he stabbed my hand with a knife and took my gun, holding it to my head—when I realized it was empty, I grabbed the syringe and jammed it into his throat, injecting him with meth.

grounded_facts: Emery Thorne retaliates against Sasha Brooks after surviving near-execution.
memories.memory_text: After Sasha Brooks disarmed me and held a gun to my head, I managed to grab the syringe from the floor and jam it into his throat, forcing the meth into him until he collapsed, then pulled it out as he choked.

grounded_facts: Taylor Hollis regains consciousness after being shot, survives momentarily with a bullet wound to the cheekbone.
After briefly reviving, Taylor Hollis dies peacefully after removing the bullet from his nose.
memories.memory_text: I saw Taylor Hollis's eyes open after he was shot, and then he put his hand to his nose and blew the bullet out into his palm. He smiled at me, embarrassed, like it was nothing. Then he just nodded, curled up on the floor like he was going to sleep, and died.

grounded_facts: Emery Thorne experiences a hallucination of a Jesse North reciting Glock specifications and shot count.
memories.memory_text: I saw a Jesse North in my mind telling me about the Glock's capacity and how many shots had been fired, like it was real.

grounded_facts: Emery Thorne shoots Taylor Hollis after Taylor Hollis attempts to leave the scene.
memories.memory_text: I shot Taylor Hollis when he tried to leave, pulling the trigger again and again even after he was down.

grounded_facts: Aftermath of violence with Taylor Hollis's revival and Emery Thorne's emotional collapse.
memories.memory_text: I saw Taylor Hollis wake up, smile at me, then curl up and die; afterward, I sat on the couch with my head in my hands, empty, and later put his gun in my mouth and kept pulling the trigger long after it was empty.

grounded_facts: After Sasha Brooks is already down, Emery Thorne empties a clip into his body and continues pulling the trigger.
memories.memory_text: I kept pulling the trigger over and over again, even after the clip was empty, just to make sure.

grounded_facts: Nico Bennett directly accuses Emery Thorne of being an informant for the police, justifying the impending violence.
memories.memory_text: I was told I was a motherfucking rat, accused of being an informant by Nico Bennett just before everything went sideways.

grounded_facts: Parker Colter explains to Emery Thorne that she betrayed him because she was forced to by threats to Tristan Hollis daughter and Tristan Hollis own safety.
memories.memory_text: I was told that Parker Colter explains to Emery Thorne that she betrayed him because she was forced to by threats to Tristan Hollis daughter and Tristan Hollis own safety.

grounded_facts: Emery Thorne realizes that Parker Colter set him up under duress, motivated by threats to Tristan Hollis daughter and Tristan Hollis own prior debt to the Pinecrest Department.

grounded_facts: The cigarette Emery Thorne dropped ignites the carpet, starting a fire that rapidly spreads through the room.
memories.memory_text: I dropped my cigarette when he shot me, and I saw it roll under the bed before the carpet caught fire and started spreading quickly.

grounded_facts: Despite being betrayed and dying, Emery Thorne comforts Parker Colter and tells Tristan Hollis to go save Tristan Hollis daughter.
memories.memory_text: I remember that Despite being betrayed and dying, Emery Thorne comforts Parker Colter and tells Tristan Hollis to go save Tristan Hollis daughter.

grounded_facts: A planned confrontation in Emery Thorne's hotel room where Nico Bennett and Parker Colter confront Emery Thorne about being an informant, resulting in violence and emotional revelation.
memories.memory_text: I remember Nico Bennett and Parker Colter confronting me in my hotel room, the gun in his hand, the way he called me a rat before shooting me, and later, Parker Colter kissing me as the fire spread.

grounded_facts: Nico Bennett uses a gun to force Parker Colter to abandon Emery Thorne as the fire spreads.
memories.memory_text: I saw Nico Bennett stop Parker Colter from coming to me, and I watched him put a gun to Tristan Hollis head and force Tristan Hollis to leave as the fire spread and she kissed me goodbye.

grounded_facts: Nico Bennett shoots Emery Thorne in the stomach, causing a severe injury and initiating a life-threatening situation.
memories.memory_text: I felt the shot in my stomach, the pain knocking me down, and later I struggled to get up, gasping for air as I staggered toward the mirror where my trumpet was.

grounded_facts: Despite his injury, Emery Thorne retrieves his trumpet and plays a few notes, then begins playing SAETA, expressing defiance or peace in his final moments.
memories.memory_text: I limped over to the bed and picked up my trumpet case, opened it, and took out the trumpet; I played a few notes, smiled, and then started to play SAETA as the fire closed in.

grounded_facts: Emery Thorne ceases playing the horn as he expresses exhaustion and relinquishes judgment about his identity.
memories.memory_text: I stopped playing the horn because I was so tired, and I told my friend to decide who I am.

grounded_facts: A tattooed likeness of Emery Thorne speaks to him during his hallucination, telling him to hang in there.
memories.memory_text: I heard my own tattoo speak to me, telling me to hang in there as I floated through the fire and hallway.

grounded_facts: Emery Thorne contemplates his past personas and declares them dead, questioning who he is now.
memories.memory_text: I told myself that both Emery Thorne and my old self are dead, and I honestly don't know who I am now.

grounded_facts: Emery Thorne calls a Avery Colter using a payphone at night.
memories.memory_text: I was told that Emery Thorne called a Avery Colter from a payphone at night and mentioned my name along with Taylor Hollis's.

grounded_facts: Sasha Brooks prompts Emery Thorne to proceed with sharing information.
memories.memory_text: I told Emery Thorne to go ahead and speak up, letting him know it was his turn.

grounded_facts: Emery Thorne indicates he does not want to speak or act in the current location due to perceived danger or lack of privacy.
memories.memory_text: I remember Emery Thorne telling me he'd rather not talk right here, saying something about not wanting to 'dish in the middle of Crankville,' like the alley was too exposed or dangerous.

grounded_facts: Sasha Brooks moves the the black jacket from the alley, responding to Emery Thorne's expressed discomfort.
memories.memory_text: I drove the the black jacket out of the alley because Emery Thorne didn't feel safe talking there, and I figured moving would help get him to open up.

grounded_facts: Sasha Brooks comments on Emery Thorne's heightened sense of danger, framing it as paranoia.
memories.memory_text: I remarked to Emery Thorne that he seemed overly paranoid tonight, questioning his heightened sense of danger.

grounded_facts: Emery Thorne defends his wariness by stating that paranoia does not preclude real threats.
memories.memory_text: I heard Emery Thorne defend his caution by saying that just because someone's paranoid doesn't mean there aren't real threats out there.

grounded_facts: Emery Thorne recalls and reveals that the suspect had a spear gun, adding new observational detail to the investigation.
memories.memory_text: I heard Emery Thorne tell me the suspect had a spear gun too.

grounded_facts: Sasha Brooks belittles Emery Thorne's observational comment by calling him an 'observant tweaker'.
memories.memory_text: I called Emery Thorne an 'observant tweaker' after he mentioned the spear gun, mocking how he just noticed that.

grounded_facts: Emery Thorne tells Sasha Brooks to be careful, clarifying that his concern is for the child involved.
memories.memory_text: Emery Thorne told me to be careful, saying he was worried about the Jesse North.

grounded_facts: Taylor Hollis violently pins Emery Thorne against the the black jacket, accusing him of cowardice and betrayal.
memories.memory_text: I saw Taylor Hollis slam Emery Thorne against the the black jacket, face to face, like he was about to break him.

grounded_facts: Taylor Hollis verbally attacks Emery Thorne, calling him a 'chickenshit tweaking snitch' and questioning his loyalty and courage.
memories.memory_text: I heard Taylor Hollis call Emery Thorne a 'chickenshit tweaking snitch' and rip into his loyalty and guts.

grounded_facts: Emery Thorne asks Sasha Brooks if he sees him as a traitor (Judas), seeking moral validation for his role as an informant.
memories.memory_text: Emery Thorne asked me if I thought he was a Judas, looking for some kind of answer about whether what he did was wrong.

grounded_facts: Sasha Brooks avoids passing moral judgment on Emery Thorne, stating it's not his place, thereby offering emotional support.
memories.memory_text: I told Emery Thorne it's not my place to judge him, and he thanked me for not passing judgment.

grounded_facts: Sasha Brooks delivers payment to Emery Thorne for his cooperation as an informant, which Emery Thorne initially refuses but eventually accepts.
memories.memory_text: I counted out several hundred-dollar bills, wrote down the serial numbers, sealed the cash in an envelope, and slid it to Emery Thorne, who eventually took it and stuffed the money into his jacket.

grounded_facts: A clandestine nighttime meeting in a deserted park where Emery Thorne, an informant, meets with detectives Sasha Brooks and Taylor Hollis to receive payment and updates about his situation.
memories.memory_text: I remember sitting across from Emery Thorne at a picnic table in a deserted park at night, with Taylor Hollis emerging from the men's room and then sitting down beside him.

memories.memory_text: I heard that threatening line through the earpiece — 'Get used to it. You're in a very tenuous position on the food chain, hoss' — and right then I thought this might be the lead we've been chasing.

grounded_facts: Taylor Hollis asks Sasha Brooks if he is thinking the same thing, implying mutual recognition of a significant lead, and Sasha Brooks confirms agreement.
memories.memory_text: Taylor Hollis turned to me after we heard it and asked if I was thinking the same thing, and I told him yes — this could be the one we're looking for.

memories.memory_text: I saw Taylor Hollis end the standoff by shocking Emery Thorne with a stun-gun, and I kicked him when he went down to assert control.

memories.memory_text: I confronted Emery Thorne in the burned-out building with Taylor Hollis, intimidating him to reveal what he knew after he tried to run. I saw Taylor Hollis use the shock gun on him and I kicked him when he fell, making sure he stayed down.

grounded_facts: Sasha Brooks tries to assert dominance by punching Emery Thorne, but fails comically due to weak strikes.
memories.memory_text: I tried to assert my dominance by punching Emery Thorne, but my strikes were so weak that he started laughing and said I hit like a girl, which made me feel humiliated instead of feared.

memories.memory_text: I was there when Emery Thorne said, 'He's the only one I told,' after someone asked about Wesley Foster, and I saw how it pointed to a breach of trust.

Sasha Brooks explicitly warns Emery Thorne that he faces federal charges and a minimum ten-year sentence unless he cooperates.
memories.memory_text: I told Emery Thorne we could take him federal for criminal conspiracy and drug distribution, and when Taylor Hollis confirmed the mandatory minimum was ten years, I made sure he knew that's exactly what he'd get unless he cooperated.

grounded_facts: Law enforcement officers interrogate Emery Thorne about his criminal associates and activities.
memories.memory_text: I paced in front of Emery Thorne and made it clear he'd face federal charges if he didn't cooperate—I told him we could go after him for ongoing criminal conspiracy and intent to distribute $250,000 worth of crank, with a mandatory ten-year sentence.

grounded_facts: Sasha Brooks rejects Emery Thorne's admission not as truth but as deception, positioning himself in opposition and escalating tension.
memories.memory_text: I didn't believe Emery Thorne when he said he was a rat—I knew he was lying, just trying to manipulate things again.

memories.memory_text: I heard Emery Thorne say he was a fucking rat, like it was some kind of badge, but I knew it was just another trick.

grounded_facts: Sasha Brooks dismisses Emery Thorne's statement and attacks his character, accusing him of thinking himself superior.
memories.memory_text: I called him out for thinking he's so smart, because that's what he always does—acts like he's better than everyone else.

grounded_facts: Sasha Brooks becomes the primary antagonist in the trio, shifting the group dynamic and increasing hostility toward Emery Thorne.
memories.memory_text: I could feel the shift in the group—I became the one standing against them, the one who had to hold the line.

grounded_facts: Sasha Brooks informs Emery Thorne that Jordan Cavendish doesn't have a Riverside School and instead robs other dealers

I thought you'd be happy, I told him.

memories.memory_text: I saw Emery Thorne fumbling under the table, trying to get to a gun he had hidden there.

memories.memory_text: I saw Robin Bellamy raise a flintlock behind Emery Thorne, but Emery Thorne dodged the shot by using the reflection in the microwave door.

memories.memory_text: I saw Emery Thorne pull the gun free and shoot Robin Bellamy twice in the chest, dropping him.

memories.memory_text: I saw Jordan Cavendish try to draw his gun, but it went off and hit his thigh, setting his pants on fire.

memories.memory_text: I entered the kitchen with Taylor Hollis and saw bodies everywhere, surveying the aftermath of the shootout with my gun still up.

memories.memory_text: I must have been mistaken when I thought I took Emery Thorne out—he stirred after I shot him, and I realized he was wearing a bulletproof vest.

memories.memory_text: I saw Emery Thorne get up and follow me and Taylor Hollis down the hallway, moving carefully behind us.

memories.memory_text: I was there with Taylor Hollis when we took down Jordan Cavendish and I helped secure the scene while he grabbed the bag of money.

memories.memory_text: Emery Thorne told me to listen carefully and forced me to imagine being shot in the shoulder, with two masked men about to kill my Sasha York — he kept demanding I answer what I would do, whether to die like a man or live to fight another day.

grounded_facts: Emery Thorne interrogates Sasha Brooks with a staged moral dilemma while he is wounded.
memories.memory_text: Emery Thorne kept yelling at me, forcing me to answer a twisted question about what I’d do if my Sasha York was about to be killed while I was shot and trapped.

memories.memory_text: I pulled my K-BAR knife from the back of my belt and stabbed Emery Thorne's gun hand to disarm him.

grounded_facts: Sasha Brooks, after gaining the upper hand, calls Emery Thorne a coward and defines his own code.
memories.memory_text: I called Emery Thorne a coward and made it clear that I fight and die like a man, that's my code.

grounded_facts: Sasha Brooks holds Emery Thorne at gunpoint and delivers a moral judgment.
memories.memory_text: I got the gun and held it to Emery Thorne's head, then told him he was a coward for how he lived and how he was going to die.

memories.memory_text: I saw Taylor Hollis somehow stand back up after being shot, bleeding and dazed, then hand his gun to Emery Thorne before curling up and dying like he was going to sleep.

grounded_facts: After emotional breakdown, Emery Thorne empties a clip into the already dying Sasha Brooks.

memories.memory_text: After Taylor Hollis let go, I remember Emery Thorne asking why he didn't help the Jesse North when he was there—said it with a sharp tone, like he was mocking him.

memories.memory_text: I heard Taylor Hollis call Emery Thorne a chickenshit tweaking snitch and a bottom feeder, tearing into him after slamming him against the the black jacket.

memories.memory_text: I pulled the wanted poster from the Cedar Grove Heights and handed it to Emery Thorne—his eyes locked onto Jordan Vale’s face, and I knew he recognized him. No more vague descriptions, just a name and a face to run with.
I slammed Adrian Keaton against the Cedar Grove Heights, face to face, and told him the truth—he’s a chickenshit snitch who wouldn’t help a Jesse North if it saved his own skin.
I didn't say a word while Adrian Keaton sat there questioning his worth, but I knew he was scared—scared of me, scared of what I think, scared of what comes next.
I pulled the earpiece out after hearing Owen Prescott tell Adrian Keaton he's in a tenuous spot on the food chain—sounded like we finally caught a break.
I watched Sasha Brooks throw those weak punches and couldn't believe it—Adrian Keaton was actually laughing. I just shook my head. This wasn't control, it was a farce.
I pulled the shock gun, zapped him in the neck, then in the crotch. When I held up the tape and told him we'd heard everything, his face went blank. He really thought he was smart.

I confirmed to Adrian Keaton we’re coordinating with Silverline Academy to monitor Jordan Cavendish—he was nervous, asking if they’d cover him if things went south. I told him, 'Don’t we always take good care of you?' and meant it as much as I ever do.

I told Adrian Keaton the red Cedar Grove Heights was registered to a 57-year-old third-grade teacher named Cameron Huxley—just to watch him unravel. Sasha Brooks and I laughed; he couldn’t even process it. Called him paranoid. Crank getting to him.
I told Emery Thorne he did good—called him a first-rate rat—after Sasha Brooks confirmed the meth was clean with the field test.

I told Emery Thorne Graham Cavendish was dead—saw the look on his face when he realized his safer option was gone and he was stuck with Owen Prescott, a fugitive who emptied fifty-seven rounds into an informant.
They talk about the drug dealers who killed Reese Finch, and I know they’re circling around me, even if they don’t say my name out loud.

I sat at the picnic table in the dark, listening to Adrian Keaton talk about giving people up, calling himself a rat—while he watched us like he was trying to decide if we were the ones who killed his Sasha York.

I ran the print from the plastic wrapper through the database and watched the screen light up with a match—Owen Prescott/Owen Prescott’s face staring back at me, just like that. It was clean, it was confirmed, and now we had our man.
They’re looking at me like I’m one of the targets now—Sasha Brooks and me, both dirty, because we didn’t report the deal. Not a word, not a trace in the system.

I heard Adrian Keaton's voice crack through the parabolic mic—'I don't have a hell of a lot of choice'—and then Owen Prescott's cold reply about being low on the food chain. I pulled the earpiece and looked at Sasha Brooks; we both knew we'd just caught the break we needed.
I finished dusting the cash for prints and asked Adrian Keaton what was on the other end of the line—he gave me the name Jordan Cavendish, a chef they should check with Silverline Academy about.

I caught the stink in the Cedar Grove Heights and called it out—'What's that smell?'—and when Adrian Keaton admitted it was him, I saw it for what it was: fear, but also a twisted kind of nerve, pissing himself after zapping Johnson and still owning it.
I told Emery Thorne we're coordinating with Silverline Academy and that we'd have his ass covered, then asked him if we don't always take good care of him—watching him squirm never gets old.
I told Emery Thorne Graham Cavendish was dead—saw the shock on his face, that flicker of something like fear or relief, hard to say which.
I took the phone back from Adrian Keaton after he finished talking to Owen Prescott, and I told him to hit the floor when we moved in—this was going to get ugly.

I watched Shawn Arden go into the building, silent beside Sasha Brooks, and when he said 'This could be the one we're looking for,' I didn't answer—just kept my eyes on the door, knowing how often 'could be' turns to nothing.
I ran the print from the plastic wrapper through the FBI database and watched it pull up Owen Prescott/Owen Prescott’s photo—match confirmed, right there on the screen.
They’re digging into the Gardena logs, and I didn’t file a report on the deal—no call, no paper trail. Not a peep.

I remember pulling the bullet from my cheek, blood all over my hand, and seeing it there—mangled, wet—like some piece of me I could just spit out. I looked at Adrian Keaton and must’ve smiled, like it was nothing, like I wasn’t falling apart.

I tried to stand, to point the gun, but my hand wouldn’t listen—my body wasn’t mine anymore. Then Adrian Keaton took the gun from me, calm as sleep, and I knew it was over. I just curled up, like lying down to rest, and let it happen.

relations.relation_summary: The relationship between Casey Nolan and Adrian Keaton Parker is defined by hostility and betrayal, stemming from Adrian Keaton's role as a secret informant who sets up a sting operation against Casey Nolan and Gus Morgan. Although they initially appear to be aligned—given Adrian Keaton’s cooperation with the corrupt cops—the evidence reveals that Adrian Keaton is actively deceiving them, turning their alliance into a one-sided trap. This deception creates a power imbalance rooted in mistrust, with Adrian Keaton manipulating the relationship to bring down Taylor Hollis. The emotional dynamic is therefore adversarial, with Taylor Hollis likely perceiving Adrian Keaton as a subordinate or ally until the betrayal is revealed. The relationship does not appear to evolve positively; instead, it collapses under the weight of Adrian Keaton’s hidden agenda. The impact on character behavior suggests that Taylor Hollis may have made decisions based on false trust, leaving him vulnerable to Adrian Keaton’s actions. The evidence is insufficient to confirm any prior camaraderie or shared history beyond the corrupt arrangement, nor is there any indication of reconciliation or direct confrontation between them in joint events.

Casey Nolan and Sasha Brooks share a complex relationship defined by deep operational collaboration juxtaposed with underlying hostility and mutual disrespect. Social relationship evidence consistently highlights their role as collaborators in both legal and criminal operations, including surveillance, tactical missions, heists, and negotiations. They are repeatedly shown coordinating actions—using shared equipment like earpieces, exchanging signals during raids, and planning operations together—indicating a high level of functional trust and synchronization in high-stakes environments. Events such as hauling a drug dealer in cuffs, entering buildings together, and preparing for criminal acts (e.g., wearing ski-masks, drawing weapons) reinforce their status as partners in joint enforcement or illicit activities. However, this cooperation is strained by evident animosity: both characters engage in derogatory language, with Taylor Hollis calling Sasha Brooks a 'first-rate rat' and Sasha Brooks mocking Taylor Hollis’s personal preferences, suggesting disdain beneath the surface. The emotional dynamic is thus one of reluctant alliance—professional coordination coexists with personal antagonism. Despite the tension, their repeated joint participation in critical operations implies a pragmatic acceptance of each other’s role, and while the relationship does not appear to evolve emotionally toward genuine camaraderie, it remains functionally resilient due to shared objectives. The evidence is insufficient to confirm whether this dynamic stems from long-standing history or situational necessity.

memories.memory_text: I asked if he had a name, and Adrian Keaton said 'Jordan Vale, rhymes with hobby'—junkie bullshit. Then he mentioned jailhouse tattoos, and Taylor Hollis slapped down a wanted poster. That was the first real confirmation.

I asked what he was holding—Adrian Keaton said eightballs, a tech knockoff in the drawer, extra mags, shotgun in the closet. Then I asked about company. He said a woman under the mattress, and there was a Jesse North. I saw the Elmo doll. That changed things.
I told Adrian Keaton it wasn't my place to judge him, and that the world just works this way — cold, but true. He looked like he needed to hear it.
I slid the envelope of cash to Adrian Keaton and told him, 'Soon. I promise,' after he asked about his situation.
I heard that voice on the mic—'tenuous position on the food chain'—and right then I knew we’d stumbled onto something real. This wasn’t just chatter; it was the break we’d been grinding for.
I called him out—'Bullshit. He's a liar.' That’s when everything shifted. I could feel the weight in the Cedar Grove Heights change, like the air got heavier.
I leaned into it—'You think you're so god damned smart, don't you?' Then I told him he played the wrong mark. I wasn't holding back anymore.
I walked out of the station with Taylor Hollis and got in the Cedar Grove Heights, nothing unusual—just another day, another shift starting.
I felt the jolt from behind—low speed, but deliberate. No one hits your bumper like that by accident.

I got the call from the Avery Colter, voice disguised, said to watch the building—then saw Shawn Arden walk in. Stood there with Taylor Hollis in the dark, and thought: this could be the one we're looking for.
I was sifting through the trunk—sawed-off shotgun, two semis, knives, gloves, ski-masks. All of it just sitting there like we were gearing up for a war.
Taylor Hollis was slapping a fake plate on the Cedar Grove Heights. I didn’t say anything—just watched him do it while I stood there with my hands in that trunk.
I pulled the Cedar Grove Heights behind the rock formation on the bluff—quiet, out of sight. Engine off, night settling in.
I felt the hit in my shoulder—sharp, hot—then I was on the floor, looking up at Adrian Keaton, trying to make sense of why he was standing over me with the gun.

I remember standing over Jordan Cavendish with Taylor Hollis, then suddenly staring down the barrel of Adrian Keaton's gun. He shot me in the shoulder. I went down. Then he told me about the bathroom, about my Sasha York—then everything got hazy.
I asked what he was holding—Adrian Keaton said a couple of eightballs, a cheap knockoff gun in the drawer with extra mags, and a gauge in the closet. That changed things.

I asked if there was any company. Adrian Keaton mentioned the woman under the mattress, then said there was a Jesse North—Elmo doll, coloring books, a silhouette through the bathroom door. I had to make sure.
I told Adrian Keaton it's not my place to judge him, and that he isn't a bad guy—just another tweaker trying to survive. He looked like he needed to hear it.
After handing over the envelope, I told him to take the money and later asked how he even got into this mess—though I didn't push when he shut it down.

I heard the voice through the earpiece—weak, filtered—Adrian Keaton saying he didn't have a choice. Then Owen Prescott's threat, cold and sharp. Taylor Hollis looked at me like we'd both just stepped on something solid. I told him yeah, this could be the one.

I told Adrian Keaton Jordan Cavendish doesn't run a Riverside School — he hits other dealers. That’s when the Jesse North realized he wasn’t setting up a buy, he was walking into a robbery.
I told him the red Cedar Grove Heights was registered to a teacher — Mrs. Cameron Huxley. The look on his face... like he’d seen a ghost. Not the monster he expected.
I held up the test kit—blue. We were in business. No doubt about it.
I pulled up Owen Prescott's file—fifty-seven bullets into an informant. Said it straight. No flinching.
I remember the yearbook photo—balding, red hair with a white streak, criminology listed under my name. Someone was looking, digging.

I felt the jolt from behind—barely a bump, but wrong. Too sudden, too clean. I turned and saw the beer cans on his front seat, Adrian Keaton just sitting there like it was routine.
We cuffed the dealer and hauled him out clean—no resistance, no mistakes. Another textbook arrest, nothing more.
I stood on the rooftop, watching Shawn Arden walk into the building—this call might actually be the break we’ve been waiting for.

memories.memory_text: I said my name was Quinn Arden, or maybe Emery Thorne—I don’t know, the names blurred together, and I could feel the fire eating through me, through the money, through the photograph of Tristan Hollis smile.

I told whoever was listening to decide what I was—trumpet player, speed Avery Foster, avenging angel, none of it mattered now, the card with 'CONGRATULATIONS!' was burning on the floor and I was just trying to make sense of it before the end.
I told Sasha Brooks to be careful, not because I care about him, but because I was actually worried about that Jesse North back there.
I played 'Saeta' on my trumpet as the sun set, and when Reese Finch said it hurt Tristan Hollis heart, I joked about being a virtuoso—then she teased me, saying Miles had the hot ass, not me.

I tackled Tristan Hollis into the sand and kept kissing Tristan Hollis, but she laughed and pushed me off, yelling 'Emery Thorne! Gross!'—then I spooned Tristan Hollis and told Tristan Hollis the song's sadness comes from imagining life without Tristan Hollis.
I remember saying 'Come on, Reese Finch. We'll get eaten alive,' but my voice didn't feel like mine—it was like I was fading, and no one could really hear me anymore.
I remember leaning forward, squinting through the windshield at that lone house glowing up the hill, and saying I’d go ask for directions—after Reese Finch told me to stop fucking around.

I snapped at Reese Finch, telling Tristan Hollis how tired I was of being reminded what a loser I am every time I messed up, and then threw in that bit about Tristan Hollis having the steady job while I'm just an unemployed musician—like I had to hand Tristan Hollis the knife to twist it deeper.
After she said not to take my low self-esteem out on Tristan Hollis, I didn't respond—just kept driving, looking ahead, and stayed silent when she called my name.

I felt the cold air hit my skin when Remy Adler yanked my pants down, and then I saw it—the weasel thrashing in the cage, eyes wild, and I knew I was going to have to put myself inside that thing or get shot.

While they were shoving me toward the cage, I pressed something into the lining of Remy Adler's jacket—don't even remember what it was now, just that I did it fast, like a reflex, hoping they wouldn't notice.
I remember standing there, hands shaking, when Sasha Huxley slammed the table and said I was spitting on Reese Finch’s grave with my drug use—like I hadn’t thought about it a thousand times already.
I called Reese Finch my Sasha York in front of that creepy guy, and she didn’t say anything—just gave me this tight look before telling me to make it fast.

I sat there with all those agents staring at me, feeling exposed when Owen Prescott said my real name and that my Sasha York had been murdered—like I was no longer just Emery Thorne, but someone they were supposed to trust with a badge.
I told him my name—Quinn Arden—standing there with the gun, watching Sasha Brooks frown like he wasn’t sure if I was real or just some ghost from the past.
I shot him in the shoulder and made him lie there, asking over and over what he would do—die a hero or save himself—while he just stared, too scared or too broken to answer.
I said my name was Quinn Arden, or maybe Emery Thorne—I didn’t know anymore, and I could feel the fire closing in, so I just let it go, asked the unseen voice to decide who I was.
I picked 'speed Avery Foster'—not because it was true, but because it was as good a label as any left, and then I started to explain the mad world of the tweaker before everything faded.
I told Sasha Brooks to be careful, and when he tried to make a joke of it, I said I was worried about the Jesse North — I meant it, even if I didn’t say it soft.
Taylor Hollis threw me against the Cedar Grove Heights and got nose-to-nose. I told him his teeth were fucking perfect. He let me go.

I tackled Reese Finch into the sand and just started kissing Tristan Hollis all over, and she was laughing, pushing me off, saying 'Emery Thorne! Gross!'—probably because of my wiener breath from that hot dog.
After playing 'Saeta' on my trumpet, I told Reese Finch that I make the song melancholy by thinking about what my life would be like without Tristan Hollis—and she just smiled and snuggled closer.
I remember squinting through the windshield, seeing that lone house up ahead, and saying I’d go ask for directions—after Reese Finch told me to stop fucking around.
I admitted I was wrong just to shut Tristan Hollis up, but it felt like swallowing glass—she loves hearing it, and I hate that I gave it to Tristan Hollis.
I snapped and threw my unemployment in Tristan Hollis face—said I was just a loser musician while she pays the bills, and it hung there, ugly and true.
I remember standing there frozen when Jordan Cavendish told me to pull my pants down, and then Robin Bellamy shoved that flintlock in my face like it was some fucked-up joke.
Remy Adler dropped my pants. Then I saw the hole where Jordan Cavendish’s nose should have been.
I remember sitting at their dining table, Cameron Huxley grabbing my wrist when I tried to leave, Tristan Hollis saying they just wanted to help me, like I was some broken thing they could fix.
I asked if the bathroom was clean, and he said it was 'kinda filthy,' then snapped at me when I tried to talk to Reese Finch—like I was stepping out of line just checking in with my own Sasha York.

I remember standing there while Owen Prescott told the room who I really was, my real name spilling out like it was evidence in a case file, and someone asking how a civilian like me could pull it off—like I wasn’t supposed to be there at all.
I said my name was Emery Thorne, Quinn Arden, and then I raised my gun and shot Sasha Brooks in the shoulder.
I shot him in the shoulder and stood over him, asking what he would do—die a hero or save himself—repeating the question until he didn't answer.
I was looking in the mirror, feeling like Emery Thorne for the first time—smoking, standing tall—until that voice said my real name, and then the shot hit my gut.
I got my revenge, and then Adrian Keaton said I was dead—like I never mattered anymore.
